Aphorism

AF-uh-riz-um · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Aphorism is short saying of a general truth.

Benjamin Franklin's aphorism that 'a penny saved is a penny earned' has guided the family's budgeting for three generations.

Worked Example

The fortune cookie's little slip of paper held a genuine aphorism about patience that the whole table quoted for weeks afterward.

Unlike a throwaway line, this saying stuck with everyone and captured something true and worth remembering -- exactly what separates a real aphorism from an empty platitude.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

maxim: A maxim is a short rule for living — practical advice you can act on, like 'measure twice, cut once.' An aphorism is broader: it states a general truth about life without necessarily telling anyone what to do. Every maxim gives guidance; an aphorism may simply observe.

adage: An adage is an old saying that has been repeated for generations until people accept it as true — its age is part of its authority. An aphorism needs no age at all: a writer can mint one this very week, and it earns its place by insight alone.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

platitude: an empty, stale remark that only sounds wise

Where it sits · how crafted and lasting the saying — observation → aphorism → proverb

observation vs. aphorism: A simple observation just notes something; an aphorism goes further, condensing that idea into a short, memorable, widely quotable form.

proverb vs. aphorism: A proverb goes further than an aphorism on this scale: an aphorism is usually traceable to one author, while a proverb has outlasted its author entirely — anonymous, and passed down for generations.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — aph- (apo-)

prefix — aph- (apo-): from/off (Greek)

root — horism

root — horism: to bound/define (Greek (horizein))

Put it together

Put it together: Apo- ('off/from') smooths to aph- before this root, plus horizein ('to define, set a boundary') gives 'a definition marked off' -- an aphorism draws a clear boundary around a truth in just a few words.

Use the root in a new word: horizon

Use the root in a new word: horizon: Horizon comes from the very same root -- the line that 'bounds' or defines where the sky meets the land or sea.
